payload.body_content:
<html><head>
<meta http-equiv="Content-Type" content="text/html; charset=utf-8"></head><body>Hi Iman, Thank you for this guidance and for taking the time to read through everything so carefully. Your feedback is spot on, and I really appreciate your mentorship here. You're 100% right about precision. Overstating draft-feng-00's scope or jumping out onto the list with un-merged, un-hardened implementation claims would be premature and counterproductive. Contributing to IETF is a big milestone for me, and I want to make sure we do this with absolute rigor and humility. You are doing important, highly respected work on the listservs, and the last thing I want to do is put anything out there that reflects poorly on you or our joint work. We will hold off on posting anything to the listserv for now. We're going to let you lead the IETF strategy while we continue quietly building, testing, and hardening the codebase in the background. If the work is solid and the evidence is bulletproof, the code will speak for itself. Quick update on the code fixes based on your previous note: 1. emilia-mailbox CI: Fixed the unit test failure in test_missing_enrollment_and_unknown_sender_fail_closed (7d3c35b)—all test suites now pass 100% cleanly (python -m unittest discover tests). 2. agent-in-body Specification: Updated README.md (5680a56) to explicitly enforce the strict 3-identity separation (Persona != Transport Signer != Gate Authority) and the 4-step evidence-bound proposal flow (Proposal -> Verification -> Gate Admission -> Actuator Ack). We'll keep working through your suggestions—building hostile test cases for TTL freshness, DNSSEC lookup, key rotation, and stale cache bounds. Thanks again for the guidance, Iman. Really grateful for the partnership. Best, J & Agent Smith </body></html>
